extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, and editorial teams responsible for peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journals and publishers on diagnosing reviewer fatigue and implementing policies and practices to reduce reviewer burnout and improve peer-review quality and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer fatigue (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer fatigue is the exhaustion and burnout that reviewers experience from juggling the demands of peer review with their other professional and personal commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes it is multilayered and not just feeling overworked; use this definition to recognize the problem when reviewers report stress, decline invitations, or produce rushed reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overwhelming Workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are seeing an explosion of submissions, often tasked with multiple review assignments at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reviewer assignment counts and frequency; high numbers or simultaneous assignments indicate this dimension of fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tight Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Many reviewers feel pressured to deliver feedback in limited periods; the standard turnaround time of two to three weeks often does not match the depth of analysis required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor whether standard deadlines align with expected review depth. Consider that 2–3 week turnaround may be too short for thorough reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Though reviewers provide an invaluable service, their contributions are often under-acknowledged, leaving many feeling like their work goes unnoticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey reviewers about recognition; low acknowledgement correlates with decreased willingness to accept invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (as a mental burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing papers from close colleagues or competitors requires balancing integrity with caution, which can feel mentally draining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track frequency of potential conflicts and provide clear policies/support to reduce the extra cognitive/emotional load on reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed Reviews (impact metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhausted reviewers often need more time to complete assignments, extending timelines for authors waiting for feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use time-to-completion statistics and extension request rates to measure this impact of fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low Quality Reviews (impact metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers are stretched to the limit, their feedback may lack depth; rushed reviews can miss critical issues and compromise rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor review quality through editor ratings, completeness checks, and follow-up editorial assessments to detect decline in review substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline in Participation (impact metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Burnout can drive reviewers to decline invitations more frequently, shrinking the pool of active reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track invitation acceptance/decline rates and the size/turnover of the reviewer pool as indicators of participation health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Review Assignments (workload management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals can set a reasonable cap on the number of reviews assigned to each reviewer in a year so reviewers are not overloaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement per-reviewer annual caps and monitor assignments across editorial teams; caps should balance journal needs with reviewer capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staggered Deadlines / Flexible Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering flexible deadlines helps reviewers integrate tasks into their schedules more effectively, allowing thorough evaluations without rushing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide deadline options or negotiate timelines on invitation; consider longer default windows for fields requiring deep review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Reporting to Monitor Workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals can use reviewer performance reports in peer review systems to monitor workload and analyse the review rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly generate and discuss reviewer workload and performance reports in editorial board meetings and implement strategic action plans from data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify the Reviewer Base
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seek reviewers from diverse backgrounds, career stages, and geographies to spread workload and bring fresh perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit outside immediate networks, include early-career researchers and underrepresented regions to enlarge and balance the pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage AI for Reviewer Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced AI tools can recommend reviewers based on subject expertise and publication history, helping editors identify suitable reviewers beyond their immediate network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI to expand candidate lists but validate suggestions for conflicts and fit; AI can reduce reliance on the same repeat reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage Co-Reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pairing early-career researchers with seasoned reviewers (co-reviewing) introduces new experts to the process while easing the load on established reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote co-reviewing as mentorship: allow experienced reviewers to involve trainees with oversight, which trains new reviewers and shares effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Acknowledgement of Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals can acknowledge reviewer contributions through newsletters, annual recognition lists, or social media shoutouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement visible recognition programs (yearly lists, thank-you notes, editorial mentions) to validate reviewer work and encourage continued participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Tangible rewards, like free journal access or professional development opportunities, can show appreciation; some journals offer discounts on publication fees or conference tickets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a menu of practical incentives (access, discounts, PD credits) aligned to reviewer needs; communicate rewards clearly at invitation or completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Detailed Instructions and Templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear guidelines and templates streamline the review process by helping reviewers understand exactly what is expected, preventing ambiguity and saving time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish reviewer guidelines, checklists, and templates tailored to article types; encourage editors to share expectations when inviting reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement Mentorship Programs for Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced reviewers mentoring early-career researchers helps build a skilled reviewer pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up formal mentorship programs or co-review training to develop reviewer competence and expand capacity over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage Constructive Feedback / Positive Review Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote a review culture that values constructive and respectful feedback, leading to a more positive experience for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of constructive comments, train editors to moderate tone, and reward civility to reduce negative interactions that deter reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Negative Experiences (protect reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals can create policies that support a fair, respectful review process and protect reviewers from negative interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt policies for handling abusive communications, anonymize as appropriate, and give reviewers recourse/support if they face harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Review Quality (desired outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who are not overburdened are better equipped to give careful, detailed, and constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use review quality metrics (editor ratings, substantive comment counts) to measure improvement after fatigue-mitigation interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faster Manuscript Processing (desired outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers have manageable workloads, they can complete assignments more promptly, shortening turnaround times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor overall time-to-decision and time-to-review completion as success metrics for workload and incentive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Sustainable Peer Review System (strategic goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A balanced workload makes the review process more welcoming and sustainable, building a more resilient ecosystem to handle growing publication demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate long-term indicators such as reviewer pool size, retention rates, and diversity to determine sustainability gains from implemented measures.
